cells.tense: You keep the picture open longer than most people would, and it fills in.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Take ten minutes with a person who is stuck in the middle of something. No verdict, no route out, no plan for them. Stay in it while it is still unresolved, and say less there than you could.
cells.core:
You can hold a whole shape and not close it. What's near you stays open longer than most people allow — you keep watching, and it fills in, week by week, without hardening into a ruling. Anyone sitting with you can feel the difference between being read and being decided about. They stay a while.

Someone close to you is working through something unfinished. Ten minutes this week, inside it with them — no verdict, no way out, no case for what they ought to do. What you understand in that time can stay under what you could say. That situation does not need your assessment yet. It can use your company.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold the whole shape and not close it.
cells.verb: seeing the whole shape of a thing while still standing inside it
cells.place: in letting go of what has already served its time

cells.tense: You will have decided what this is before it finishes saying what it is.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: Before the week ends, turn down one invitation you would normally half-accept out of habit. No reasons filed, no case for it, no apology attached. Just the no.
cells.core:
You take the whole shape in early, and once it is in, you start holding the picture against the reality. Somebody's situation becomes the version you drew of it, and they arrive already decided about. It reads as clarity from inside. From the other chair it reads as a verdict handed down before they finished.

One week, one clear turning-down. Not a thing that deserves refusal — an invitation you would have half-accepted without noticing. Turn it down and mean it, no reasons filed. You can want what you want without first proving they had it coming. A picture can be held without being announced.
cells.sheetLine: The picture you drew is now the verdict they hear.

cells.tense: You stood at the door a long time and it was behind you before you moved.
cells.act: open the thing you have been assuming you knew and look at it unlabelled
cells.ask: Take a person you hold a settled read on and spend a few minutes with them like a stranger would. Keep whatever shows up that your usual read skips past, and keep it to yourself.
cells.core:
Meeting anything freshly has gone quiet. What you do now is review — you come to a person or a situation under a heading, and the heading answers before the meeting does. Nothing gets past it and nothing needs to. The open look you once brought to things has been replaced by the file you already keep.

Take someone with a settled place in your mind. Spend a few minutes with them the way a stranger would — no heading, no summary, no file. Keep whatever shows up that your usual read skips. You do not have to be wrong about what you think. Only let yourself meet something again somewhere, and this is somewhere.
cells.sheetLine: You meet the heading and the meeting is over.

cells.tense: You are reading the situation correctly and have not signed your name to the reading.
cells.act: give back what is owed, and take what is yours
cells.ask: When someone thanks you for understanding what they were going through, let it land. Say thanks, once, and stop there — do not hand the credit to luck or to the obviousness of the situation.
cells.core:
Something keeps arriving in you and going under other names. A conversation opens and you have the shape of where it is going. You credit the other person for asking well, or the situation for being plain. Your eye got there first, and the credit goes somewhere else.

Let an exchange finish the way it started. Someone thanks you for understanding what they were carrying — say thanks, once, and take it. No handing it to luck, no naming how obvious the thing was. Taking what is owed is not vanity. It is what understanding looks like when you stop calling it the situation's.
cells.sheetLine: Your eye gets there first and the credit goes elsewhere.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: I say the person already senses the shape of something and has not put their name on it — the record supports the abstract capacity, not that it is currently active. The reader could reasonably say this is just flattery for a skill they do not have; and for the Balanced cell I say the seeing is deepening when the record only permits it. The asks survive being wrong: each is small, standalone, and teaches something whether or not the read lands. The sentence serving me more than them: none I would keep — the strongest risk is in the Too Much core saying the person's rightness is ageing badly, which I have narrowed to the moment and not to them.
